# Temple Scroll Column 49 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 49 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 49:2 — rhetorical question phrasing — tree/man comparison

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "is a tree of the field a man, that it should be besieged by you?" | Traditional formulation |
| LOGOS | "is the tree of the field a human being, that it should come under your siege?" | Gender-neutral formal |
| PNEUMA | "Trees are not your enemies; why make war on them?" | Restatement as declaration |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's traditional rhetorical question. The interrogative form is faithful to the Hebrew and more rhetorically effective.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:5 — "indecent thing" vs. "indecent matter" vs. "anything offensive" — ervat davar

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "any indecent thing" | Literal ervat davar |
| LOGOS | "any indecent matter" | Formal synonym |
| PNEUMA | "anything offensive" | Simplified modern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "indecent thing" per EMET. Closer to the Hebrew construction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:9 — "weep" vs. "mourn" vs. "mourn" — bakah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "weep for her father and her mother" | Literal bakah — to weep |
| LOGOS | "mourn her father and her mother" | Broader term |
| PNEUMA | "mourn her father and mother" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "weep" per EMET. Bakah specifically means to weep/cry, not merely to mourn. The image of weeping is more vivid and accurate.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:12 — "as a slave" vs. "as merchandise" vs. "as property" — hit'ammer rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall not treat her as a slave" | Interpretation of hit'ammer |
| LOGOS | "you shall not treat her as merchandise" | Commercial connotation |
| PNEUMA | "you must not treat her as property" | Modern rights language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "as a slave" per EMET. The verb hit'ammer likely relates to servitude/exploitation, and "slave" connects to the preceding prohibition on selling.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:12 — "humbled" vs. "humiliated" vs. "taken her dignity" — innah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you have humbled her" | Literal innah |
| LOGOS | "you have humiliated her" | Stronger connotation |
| PNEUMA | "you have taken her dignity" | Interpretive expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "humbled" per EMET. Innah means to humble/afflict — consistent with project convention (cf. Leviticus ve-innitem rulings).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:15 — "consecrated woman/man" vs. "cult devotee" vs. "temple prostitute" — qedeshah/qadesh

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "consecrated woman" / "consecrated man" | Project convention from Gen 38 |
| LOGOS | "cult devotee" / "cult devotee" | Religiously neutral term |
| PNEUMA | "temple prostitute" / "temple prostitute" | Traditional interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "consecrated woman/man" per EMET and project convention established in Genesis 38:21-22.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 49:16 — "price of a dog" vs. "wages of a male prostitute" vs. explicit rendering — kelev euphemism

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the price of a dog" | Preserves Hebrew euphemism |
| LOGOS | "the wages of a male prostitute" | Interprets the euphemism |
| PNEUMA | "money earned through prostitution — whether by a woman or a man" | Fully explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the price of a dog" per EMET. Preserving the Hebrew euphemism is consistent with the project's approach to culturally embedded language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
